name: AlphaRAR.respMG
doc:
Centered response martingale of a fixed arm,
`Q n = ∑_{j<n} X j (ξ j - θ)`.

statement.value: ∑ j ∈ Finset.range n, X j * (ξ j - θ)

specifiedBy.comment: what `Q` is for: divided by the count it is exactly the sample-mean error, so every rate proved for `Q` is a rate for the estimator
the centring is applied once per *pull*, not once per patient: `Q` subtracts `θ` times the count `N n`, not `θ n`

name: AlphaRAR.theta_error_Q
doc:
**Estimator error via `Q`**.

On `{N n ≠ 0}`, the leading term of the estimator error equals `Q n / N n`:
`(∑ X ξ) / N n - θ = Q n / N n`.

statement.conclusion: (∑ j ∈ Finset.range n, X j * ξ j) / count X n - θ = respMG X ξ θ n / count X n

code:
/-- **Estimator error via `Q`**.

On `{N n ≠ 0}`, the leading term of the estimator error equals `Q n / N n`:
`(∑ X ξ) / N n - θ = Q n / N n`. -/
@[specifies respMG "what `Q` is for: divided by the count it is exactly the sample-mean error, so \
every rate proved for `Q` is a rate for the estimator"]
lemma theta_error_Q (ξ : ℕ → ℝ) (θ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (hN : count X n ≠ 0) :
    (∑ j ∈ range n, X j * ξ j) / count X n - θ = respMG X ξ θ n / count X n
proof:
:= by
  rw [respMG_eq, sub_div, mul_div_assoc, div_self hN, mul_one]

specifies.comment: what `Q` is for: divided by the count it is exactly the sample-mean error, so every rate proved for `Q` is a rate for the estimator

name: AlphaRAR.respMG_eq
doc: `Q n = ∑ X ξ - θ N n`: the response martingale rewritten via the count.

statement.conclusion: respMG X ξ θ n = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range n, X j * ξ j - θ * count X n

code:
/-- `Q n = ∑ X ξ - θ N n`: the response martingale rewritten via the count. -/
@[specifies respMG "the centring is applied once per *pull*, not once per patient: `Q` subtracts \
`θ` times the count `N n`, not `θ n`"]
lemma respMG_eq (ξ : ℕ → ℝ) (θ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    respMG X ξ θ n = (∑ j ∈ range n, X j * ξ j) - θ * count X n
proof:
:= by
  unfold respMG count
  rw [Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro j _
  ring

specifies.comment: the centring is applied once per *pull*, not once per patient: `Q` subtracts `θ` times the count `N n`, not `θ n`

name: AlphaRAR.estimator
doc:
Sequential estimator of a fixed arm, equation (1) of the paper:
`θ̂ n = (∑_{j<n} X j ξ j + θ₀) / (N n + 1)`, with initial value `θ₀` and the `+1`
regularization in the denominator.

statement.value: (∑ j ∈ Finset.range n, X j * ξ j + θ₀) / (count X n + 1)

code:
/-- Sequential estimator of a fixed arm, equation (1) of the paper:
`θ̂ n = (∑_{j<n} X j ξ j + θ₀) / (N n + 1)`, with initial value `θ₀` and the `+1`
regularization in the denominator. -/
noncomputable def estimator (ξ : ℕ → ℝ) (θ₀ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ((∑ j ∈ range n, X j * ξ j) + θ₀) / (count X n + 1)

specifiedBy.comment: accounts exactly for the `+θ₀` / `+1` regularization: it contributes the single constant `θ₀ - θ` to the numerator and nothing else, so the regularized estimator has the same error expansion as the plain sample mean with no remainder term

name: AlphaRAR.estimator_sub_eq
doc:
**Exact estimator error**, the exact form of the Bahadur representation.

The regularized estimator has the *exact* error decomposition
`θ̂ n - θ = (Q n + (θ₀ - θ)) / (N n + 1)`, valid whenever `N n + 1 ≠ 0` (always, for
`{0,1}`-valued assignment indicators). Since `Q n = O(√(n \log n))` and the numerator offset
`θ₀ - θ` is constant, this is the Bahadur representation of equation (2) of the paper,
`θ̂ n = \tfrac1{N n}∑ X ξ + o(N n^{-1/2})`, in sharp, remainder-free form.

statement.conclusion: estimator X ξ θ₀ n - θ = (respMG X ξ θ n + (θ₀ - θ)) / (count X n + 1)

code:
/-- **Exact estimator error**, the exact form of the Bahadur representation.

The regularized estimator has the *exact* error decomposition
`θ̂ n - θ = (Q n + (θ₀ - θ)) / (N n + 1)`, valid whenever `N n + 1 ≠ 0` (always, for
`{0,1}`-valued assignment indicators). Since `Q n = O(√(n \log n))` and the numerator offset
`θ₀ - θ` is constant, this is the Bahadur representation of equation (2) of the paper,
`θ̂ n = \tfrac1{N n}∑ X ξ + o(N n^{-1/2})`, in sharp, remainder-free form. -/
@[specifies estimator "accounts exactly for the `+θ₀` / `+1` regularization: it contributes the \
single constant `θ₀ - θ` to the numerator and nothing else, so the regularized estimator has the \
same error expansion as the plain sample mean with no remainder term"]
lemma estimator_sub_eq (ξ : ℕ → ℝ) (θ θ₀ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (hN : count X n + 1 ≠ 0) :
    estimator X ξ θ₀ n - θ = (respMG X ξ θ n + (θ₀ - θ)) / (count X n + 1)

specifies.comment: accounts exactly for the `+θ₀` / `+1` regularization: it contributes the single constant `θ₀ - θ` to the numerator and nothing else, so the regularized estimator has the same error expansion as the plain sample mean with no remainder term
